description: The Kubernetes view (Baude's and Record's): a cluster's objects, a page of each kind, an object's YAML and a pod's logs.

messages.not_on_path: kubectl signs in to this cluster with {$program}, which isn't on Baude's PATH ({$path})
messages.credentials_refused: The cluster didn't accept your credentials
messages.namespaces_tip: Namespaces shown (any of them at once)
messages.copied_try_again: Copied: run it in a terminal, then Try Again
messages.previous_tip: Its previous run's log (one that crashed, say), instead of this one's
messages.follow_tip: Follow: keep to the newest line (scrolling up stops it, scrolling to the end again goes on)
messages.cant_watch: can't watch {$kind} ({$why}): read every {$seconds} s instead
messages.metrics: CPU and memory from the metrics API, every {$seconds} s
messages.no_metrics: no metrics API on this cluster (CPU and memory N/A)
messages.no_containers: {$pod} has no containers to show logs of
messages.remote_cluster: This is a remote cluster: {$context}'s API server isn't on this machine.
messages.force_delete_body: Force delete doesn't wait for the pod to stop: the cluster forgets it at once, while its containers may go on running on their node for a while.
messages.delete_body: Its containers are stopped, given their grace period to finish.
messages.controlled_by: It's controlled by {$kind} {$name}, which may start another in its place.
messages.no_controller: No controller owns it: nothing will start it again.
messages.allocatable_tip: What the nodes can give pods (their allocatable)
messages.requested_tip: What the pods ask for: their containers' requests
messages.used_tip: What the pods use now, from the metrics API
messages.limits_tip: What the pods are held to: their containers' limits, where they set one
messages.history_tip: Used (and requested, dashed) over the last {$minutes} minutes
